title: window
summary: An everyday opening with a surprisingly poetic name.
question: Where did this word come from?
completion: English window ← a Norse word related to Old Norse vindauga, “wind-eye”. The exact first spoken form borrowed into English was not recorded.
partner: A similar sound is a clue. Let’s check the evidence.

evidence.title: An Old Norse clue
evidence.text: Vindr means wind. Auga means eye. This Old Norse word paints a picture: a “wind-eye”. English window belongs to this northern story.
evidence.notice: Imagine an opening that lets wind into a house. Why might someone call it a wind-eye? The exact spoken form first borrowed into English was not recorded.
